ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is dark brown or blackish above with a yellowish belly. Key features include a blunt, rounded head and small eyes with vertically elliptical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dieurostus dussumieri* is best distinguished by its distinctively blunt, rounded snout and the presence of a single internasal scale, unlike the divided scales of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Dieurostus dussumieri* inhabits low-altitude freshwater wetlands, marshes, and paddy fields, typically found in the coastal plains of Kerala and southwestern India.
ai.behavior: The Kerala Mud Snake is primarily nocturnal and semi-aquatic, often remaining submerged in muddy substrates to ambush small fish and amphibians.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Kerala Mud Snake is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with litters typically consisting of 3–8 offspring.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dieurostus dussumieri* is endemic to the coastal lowlands of Kerala and southwestern Tamil Nadu, typically found in wetlands and paddy fields below 200 meters.
